idiom_name: single-threaded agent (event loop) - confinement by construction; postMessage/structuredClone to cross to workers
implementation_notes: Every agent - the main program and each worker - executes JavaScript on a single thread, so an object created inside one agent is confined to it by construction: there are no locks, and none are needed. Crossing to another agent is explicit and copy-based: `postMessage`/`structuredClone` serialize the object, so the receiver gets its own instance (confinement by transfer), and the only genuine escape hatch is `SharedArrayBuffer`, which is shared memory and requires `Atomics` to synchronize. The classic per-thread slot structure has no JS counterpart and none is needed; the modern analogue for ambient per-operation state is Node's `AsyncLocalStorage` (`node:async_hooks`), which keeps a store across the callbacks and promises of one async operation rather than one thread.
pitfalls: Structured clone copies only cloneable values: functions, DOM nodes and class instances lose their prototype, and the receiver's object is a different instance - sharing assumptions break at the boundary.
SharedArrayBuffer (secure context and cross-origin isolated only) reintroduces real shared memory; it is the one way out of confinement and needs Atomics for ordering.
Confinement means one thread does everything: a long synchronous computation blocks the whole agent, so heavy work belongs in a worker, not in a bigger critical section.
